{The king, at his third square.} 6. Kd4 {The king, at his queen's fourth square.} Kd6 {The king,
at his queen's third square. (d) NOTE: In this position he has got the move over you, since he
may oppose your king, but by the sacrifice of a pawn you may recover it over him, and a single
pawn is enough to win the game.} 7. f7 {The king's bishop's pawn, one move.} Ke7 {The king, at
his second square.} 8. Ke5 {The king, at the adverse king's fourth square.} Kxf7 {The king takes
